notes: PARENTAGE AND MARRIAGE DOCUMENTED (research 2026-07-04, part of resolving spouse Garrett Groff's impossible-lifespan flag): Amy Stratton is documented as a daughter of David Stratton (b. 1714/15, Evesham, Burlington Co., NJ; d. 11 Jun 1771, Evesham; tailor, prominent Quaker) and Mary Elkinton (b. 2 Nov 1714; d. 21 Feb 1808), who married 7 Jan 1736/37 at the meetinghouse in Chester Township (now Moorestown), NJ -- per WikiTree Stratton-419 and markstratton.org's 'Family History of Mark Stratton,' both listing 'Amy (Stratton) Groff' among the couple's eight children. [documented -- parentage]

Her marriage is independently documented: William Nelson, ed., 'New Jersey Marriage Records, 1665-1800' (Archives of the State of New Jersey, First Series, Vol. XXII, 1900), transcribed at newhorizonsgenealogicalservices.com, records 'Groff, Garret, and Amy Stratton, of Burlington Co., 11-15-1764'; WikiTree/markstratton.org corroborate from her side ('married Garrot Goff (Groff) of Salem on November 15, 1764'). This confirms her husband was a real 'Garret/Garrett Groff of Salem,' matching I182381535298. [documented -- marriage]

Her own birth year (1741, tree-supplied, unsourced) is plausible but not independently confirmed -- it falls within her parents' 1737-1771 childbearing span and would make her about 23 at her 1764 wedding, an ordinary bridal age. Her death (1835, Burlington, NJ) likewise remains unsourced. See docs/research/ancestors/gen09-garrett-groff.md.
